question.text: A Market Maker in commodity derivatives is obligated to:

answer.text: Provide two-way quotes at all times to maintain liquidity
Take physical delivery of all commodity contracts
Guarantee profits to other market participants
Set the daily settlement price for the exchange

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook defines a Market Maker as a class of members obligated to provide liquidity by giving two-way (buy and sell) quotes at all times as prescribed by the exchange. The Trap: Market makers are not required to take physical delivery, do not guarantee profits to other participants and do not set the daily settlement price, which is determined by the exchange. Note: The source-supported obligation is two-way quoting for liquidity; no further claims about market-maker compensation are added here.
